jobs.title: Solutions Lead, Healthcare
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview:

We are building Protege to solve the biggest unmet need in AI — getting access to the right training data. The process today is time intensive, incredibly expensive, and often ends in failure. The Protege platform facilitates the secure, efficient, and privacy-centric exchange of AI training data.

Solving AI’s data problem is a generational opportunity. We’re backed by world-class investors and already powering partnerships with some of the most ambitious teams in AI. The company that succeeds will be one of the largest in AI — and in tech.

We’re a lean, fast-moving, high-trust team of builders who are obsessed with velocity and impact. Our culture is built for people who thrive on ambiguity, own outcomes, and want to shape the future of data and AI.

Role Overview

We're hiring a Healthcare Solutions Lead to guide prospects and customers through the definition and delivery of healthcare datasets. This is a customer-facing, technically grounded role that sits at the intersection of solution design, program delivery, and data quality.

Your job is to understand what customers are building, identify the healthcare data that best fits their needs, and assemble high-quality samples and final deliveries that meet both technical and conceptual requirements. You will operate across modalities including EHR, claims, radiology, pathology, and unstructured text, while keeping timelines, milestones, and risks clear from feasibility through final handoff.

At its core, this role is about creating clarity in ambiguous situations: translating customer needs into a structured plan, coordinating the right internal and external partners, and ensuring the final dataset is both usable and trustworthy.

What You'll Do

Lead solution design and customer delivery

  • Translate customer requirements into clear dataset plans, delivery scopes, milestones, and execution paths.

  • Serve as a primary customer contact, managing expectations and keeping technical decisions legible throughout the process.

  • Lead end-to-end program management from initial specification through QA, packaging, and final delivery.

Own the technical and analytical work behind delivery

  • Use SQL and Python to construct cohorts, evaluate data readiness, validate coverage, and support customer-specific requirements.

  • Assess tradeoffs across modalities, sources, and delivery approaches to determine what is feasible and highest-value.

  • Create structured plans that connect solution architecture, partner constraints, privacy requirements, and delivery execution.

Drive quality, compliance, and partner coordination

  • Oversee QA for complex healthcare datasets, including EHR, claims, radiology, pathology, and unstructured text.

  • Work with Protege data partners to source and refine healthcare datasets needed for active opportunities and deliveries.

  • Partner with privacy stakeholders to ensure HIPAA-aware handling and appropriate safeguards throughout the delivery process.

Create leverage for the team

  • Bring order to multiple simultaneous projects and keep priorities, risks, and dependencies visible.

  • Identify repeatable improvements to planning, QA, communication, and delivery workflows.

  • Help the team get better at moving quickly without losing rigor, trust, or customer clarity.

What Success Looks Like

  • 30 days: Learn the system. Build a strong understanding of the healthcare delivery motion, the core modalities, the partner network, and the biggest execution risks in the current process.

  • 60 days: Own meaningful work. Run live customer or delivery workstreams with clear plans, credible QA, and strong cross-functional coordination.

  • 90 days: Create leverage. Independently manage complex healthcare opportunities while improving the operating rhythm, the quality bar, and the team's ability to scale.

What You Bring

  • Strong customer-facing experience and comfort leading technical conversations with clarity and confidence.

  • Analyst-first mindset with deep hands-on fluency in SQL and Python for cohorting, coverage analysis, and data-readiness work.

  • Deep familiarity with healthcare data modalities such as EHR, claims, radiology, pathology, and unstructured text.

  • Experience bringing order to multiple simultaneous projects with changing priorities and real deadlines.

  • Familiarity with privacy-preserving techniques and the practical quality requirements of healthcare data delivery.

  • Experience in healthcare AI, ML products, enterprise data platforms, or similarly technical healthcare environments.

  • Startup comfort, strong ownership, and a high bar for kindness and follow-through.

Working with Protege

  • We move fast - thoughtfully. Speed matters in what we're building, and so does intention. We're biased toward action and always learning.

  • We're a lean, high-trust team. Everyone has real ownership. Clarity and autonomy drive our best work.

  • We take our work seriously, not ourselves. We solve hard problems with humility and celebrate wins - big and small.

  • We're kind, direct, and inclusive. We give feedback early and often, with the goal of helping one another grow.

  • We're builders at heart. Every person at Protege is hands-on, resourceful, and focused on creating momentum.

  • We grow fast - together. You'll be surrounded by people who care about impact, who challenge you to think bigger, and who are genuinely excited about what comes next.

Protege Values

Pass the Loved Ones’ Test
We act with integrity and do the right thing — especially when it’s hard and no one is watching.


Always Find a Way
We are resourceful, resilient builders who solve hard problems and push through obstacles.


Go Fast and Grow Fast
Velocity matters. We move with urgency, learn quickly, and continuously improve as individuals and as a company.


Practice Kindness and Candor
We communicate directly and respectfully, building trust through honest feedback and genuine care for one another.

Deliver Together
We win as one team. Collaboration, accountability, and shared ownership drive our success.

Own the Outcome. Hone the Craft.
We take pride in our work, sweat the details, and continuously raise the bar for excellence.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Healthcare
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview:

We’re a lean, fast-moving, high-trust team of builders who are obsessed with velocity and impact. Our culture is built for people who thrive on ambiguity, own outcomes, and want to shape the future of data and AI.

Role Overview

Protege is hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer, Healthcare to own customer-facing technical engagements from initial scoping through post-engagement support.

This role sits at the intersection of software engineering, solution architecture, and customer partnership. The person in this seat will build custom solutions, navigate healthcare data environments, and translate customer needs into practical technical execution across Protege’s product and platform.

As Protege expands its healthcare business, customers and data partners need tailored implementation support and technical expertise in complex, regulated environments. This role is critical to accelerating customer and data partner outcomes, ensuring success across a growing portfolio of engagements, and identifying repeatable implementation patterns that can become scalable product capabilities.

This role sits at the center of a vertical that is growing extremely rapidly. You'll be managing customer and partner relationships, technical engagements, and architecture decisions at the same time. The pace is fast, the ambiguity is real, and when deals are live, availability outside standard hours is part of the job. If this type of environment and growth excites you, there could be a strong fit. If this is not something you are actively looking for, this likely is not the correct role.

What You’ll Do

Own healthcare customer engagements end-to-end

  • Lead technical work from initial scoping through implementation, data ingestion, and continued refreshes.

  • Become the primary technical partner for assigned healthcare data partners.

  • Build trusted relationships with customer engineering and technical teams.

  • Manage multiple concurrent healthcare engagements while maintaining quality and customer confidence.

Build custom solutions for complex customer needs

  • Develop and deploy integrations, data transformations, and applications that solve customer-specific challenges.

  • Navigate customer technical environments and adapt Protege’s platform capabilities to real-world deployment constraints.

  • Translate ambiguous customer needs into clear technical plans, milestones, and practical implementation paths.

Bridge customer needs with product and platform capabilities

  • Identify where customer-specific work points to repeatable product opportunities.

  • Surface actionable product feedback based on implementation patterns, customer pain points, and blockers.

  • Partner with product and engineering to turn bespoke solutions into reusable platform capabilities where appropriate.

Operate with strong healthcare data judgment

  • Handle healthcare data environments with appropriate care, including PHI and regulatory considerations.

  • Make sound technical decisions in complex, regulated settings.

  • Communicate clearly with customers and internal teams about tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, and implementation choices.

Create reusable leverage

  • Contribute playbooks, tooling, templates, and best practices that improve future healthcare deal execution.

  • Document repeatable patterns and lessons from customer engagements.

  • Help Protege move faster over time by turning one-off implementation work into reusable assets.

What Success Looks Like

30 days: Support an active deal

  • The FDE has built context on Protege’s healthcare customer motion, platform capabilities, common implementation needs, and regulated data considerations. They are supporting an active customer engagement with guidance.

60 days: Manages multiple customer engagements

  • The FDE is independently leading a scoped customer engagement or technical workstream, building trust with customer technical teams, and delivering against customer requirements and timelines.

90 days: Owns multiple concurrent engagements

  • The FDE is independently managing multiple healthcare customer engagements, contributing reusable playbooks or tooling, and surfacing product feedback that helps convert bespoke implementation patterns into scalable capabilities.

What You Bring

  • Experience in software engineering, solution architecture, forward deployed engineering, technical implementation, or a similar customer-facing technical role.

  • Ability to own customer engagements from scoping to repeated support.

  • Strong technical execution across custom solutions, integrations, data transformations, and/or applications.

  • Comfort operating in healthcare data environments, including sensitivity to PHI and regulatory considerations.

  • Strong customer-facing communication and ability to build trust with technical stakeholders.

  • Ability to bridge customer needs with product and platform capabilities.

  • High ownership, adaptability, and comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

  • Bias toward creating reusable systems, playbooks, tooling, and best practices rather than solving the same problem repeatedly.

We are resourceful, resilient builders who solve hard problems and push through obstacles.

About Protege

We are building Protege to solve the biggest unmet need in AI - getting access to the right training data. The process today is time intensive, incredibly expensive, and often ends in failure. The Protege platform facilitates the secure, efficient, and privacy-centric exchange of AI training data.

Solving AI's data problem is a generational opportunity. We're backed by world-class investors and already powering partnerships with some of the most ambitious teams in AI. The company that succeeds will be one of the largest in AI - and in tech.

We're a lean, fast-moving, high-trust team of builders who are obsessed with velocity and impact. Our culture is built for people who thrive on ambiguity, own outcomes, and want to shape the future of data and AI.

 

DataLab is Protege's research arm - a team of research scientists committed to tackling the fundamental challenges and open questions regarding data for AI. We bridge the gap between research theory and data deployment to push the frontier forward, publishing on the questions that matter: what agentic AI should actually be trained to do, how to quality-control large-scale corpora, and how to build evaluation datasets that reflect the real world rather than the leaderboard.

We're a lean, fast-moving, high-trust team of builders who deeply care about scientific rigor and impact. Our culture is built for people who thrive on ambiguity, own outcomes, and want to shape the future of data and AI.

The Role

The Head of Research will lead Protege's DataLab as a strategic research function focused on answering the hardest questions about data for AI. This person will define the research agenda, build rigorous systems for experimentation and evaluation, and ensure DataLab's work directly informs product direction, customer strategy, and platform capabilities.

This is both a leadership and builder role. The right person can set a clear research roadmap, manage and scale a high-performing team, partner across Product, Engineering, GTM, and Leadership, and translate ambiguous technical questions into practical frameworks, measurable experiments, and actionable recommendations.

The Director of Research will work closely with GTM across sales, delivery, and partner conversations — bringing technical credibility into the room when it matters and representing Protege’s research perspective externally.

What You'll Do

  • Define and lead the research strategy for Protege's Data Lab, aligning experimentation with company priorities and product direction.

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams to identify high-value research opportunities tied to AI data quality, evaluation, and marketplace performance.

  • Design and oversee experiments that evaluate dataset quality, model performance, synthetic data workflows, and privacy-preserving methodologies.

  • Build scalable systems for benchmarking, labeling quality analysis, and training data evaluation across multiple AI modalities.

  • Serve as a customer-facing research partner to GTM, representing DataLab in sales, technical discovery, delivery, and customer strategy conversations while translating research depth into practical guidance that helps Protege deliver value to our partners and customers.

  • Translate ambiguous technical questions into clear research frameworks, measurable hypotheses, and actionable recommendations.

  • Publish internal research findings that directly influence product decisions, customer strategy, and platform capabilities.

  • Lead, manage, and scale a high-performing team of researchers and data scientists, driving execution, technical excellence, and career development across the Data Lab organization.

  • Establish operational rigor around experimentation, reproducibility, and research documentation.

  • Represent Protege externally through technical conversations with customers, partners, and the broader AI ecosystem.

  • Stay at the forefront of advancements in foundation models, evaluation methodologies, data infrastructure, and AI alignment research.

What Success Looks Like

30 Days: Learn and Assess

  • Build a deep understanding of Protege's platform, customer workflows, and current research priorities.

  • Meet cross-functional stakeholders across Product, Engineering, GTM, and Leadership to understand strategic goals and existing technical challenges.

  • Audit current Data Lab workflows, experimentation infrastructure, and evaluation methodologies.

  • Identify immediate opportunities to improve research velocity, rigor, and cross-functional communication.

60 Days: Establish Direction and Build Momentum

  • Deliver a clear research roadmap aligned to company priorities and platform differentiation.

  • Launch initial experiments focused on data quality, evaluation systems, or marketplace optimization.

  • Introduce standardized processes for experiment tracking, documentation, and reproducibility.

  • Develop hiring plans and organizational structure for scaling the Data Lab function.

90 Days: Drive Measurable Impact

  • Deliver research insights that directly influence product roadmap decisions or customer outcomes.

  • Demonstrate measurable improvements in experimentation speed, evaluation quality, or data performance metrics.

  • Establish Protege's Data Lab as a trusted strategic partner across Engineering, Product, and GTM.

  • Recruit, onboard, and effectively lead key technical talent to support long-term research initiatives and company growth.

What we're looking for

You have:

  • Led impactful research initiatives in AI, machine learning, data infrastructure, or applied research environments where outcomes influenced product or business strategy.

  • Built and managed high-performing research teams that operated with autonomy, technical rigor, and fast execution cycles.

  • Experience partnering directly with customers, GTM teams, or external stakeholders in applied technical settings, with the judgment to represent both the research and business value of complex AI/data work clearly and credibly.

  • Developed frameworks for evaluating model performance, dataset quality, synthetic data, or large-scale experimentation systems.

  • Experience operating in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where priorities evolved quickly and execution mattered.

  • Strong ability to communicate complex technical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Demonstrated ownership of cross-functional initiatives spanning research, engineering, product, and go-to-market teams.

  • Track record of translating research into practical systems, tools, or customer-facing impact.

  • Experience working with modern AI systems, foundation models, LLM evaluation workflows, or privacy-centric data methodologies.

  • High judgment, strong prioritization skills, and comfort making decisions with incomplete information.

  • Motivated by building from first principles and solving foundational problems in AI infrastructure.

Protege's Values

We act with integrity and do the right thing - especially when it's hard and no one is watching.

Always Find a Way

We are resourceful, resilient builders who solve hard problems and push through obstacles.

Go Fast and Grow Fast

Velocity matters. We move with urgency, learn quickly, and continuously improve as individuals and as a company.

Practice Kindness and Candor

We communicate directly and respectfully, building trust through honest feedback and genuine care for one another.

Deliver Together

We win as one team. Collaboration, accountability, and shared ownership drive our success.

Own the Outcome. Hone the Craft.

We take pride in our work, sweat the details, and continuously raise the bar for excellence.

Role Overview

We are hiring Applied Healthcare Researchers to join a team within DataLab focused entirely on healthcare training data.

Our customers are researchers at the frontier labs and AI startups building specialized healthcare models. They come to us with model-development problems, not dataset specifications. Figuring out which healthcare data actually solves their problem, and proving that it does, is the research question we answer in DataLab.

In this role you will work directly with researchers at those labs to understand what they're trying to train or evaluate, determine what healthcare data can support it, and do the research needed to demonstrate that it will. This is fast-iterating, customer-facing research on a customer's timeline. You will be the primary technical and research link to the customer — not a technical resource brought in for credibility, but the person driving the conversation and pulling in the solutions, engineering, and data partnerships teams as needed.

Core Responsibilities

Customer Research Partnership

You will be the research partner to AI researchers at frontier labs and startups who are working on healthcare problems.

• Serve as the primary technical and research point of contact for healthcare customer conversations.

• Translate a lab's model-development goals into concrete, feasible data strategies.

• Help customers scope opportunities and identify the highest-value data available to them.

• Explain data limitations, tradeoffs, and potential biases to technically sophisticated stakeholders while grounding conversations in what real-world data actually looks like.

• After delivery, answer the research questions customers raise about the data we provided. Delivery is not the end of the relationship.

Applied Research & Method Development

Curating the right data product is a research problem, and you'll own solving it.

• Develop and evaluate methods — fine-tuning, LLM-based extraction, classification, rules-based approaches, or whatever the problem calls for — to demonstrate that a dataset can support a customer's training or evaluation objective.

• Design and run feasibility research pre-contract: can this data support this model objective, at what quality, with what caveats.

• Build the evidence base that makes a data strategy credible — benchmarks, validation analyses, error characterization, and honest assessments of where the data falls short.

• Partner with the Assessments team on healthcare benchmarks across modalities.

Data Feasibility & Dataset Strategy

• Evaluate whether requested variables, labels, or cohort definitions are achievable with available healthcare data.

• Identify proxy variables or alternative dataset structures when the ideal variable doesn't exist.

• Analyze partner and source datasets — schema, field availability, quality, completeness, and required transformations.

• Contribute to our point of view on which healthcare data matters most for which modality and which stage of model development.

• Help evaluate new data partners and identify datasets worth acquiring before a customer asks for them.

Reusable Research & Scaling

• Produce reusable research, evidence, and technical collateral rather than starting from scratch for each opportunity.

• Identify where a successful one-off approach should become a repeatable workflow, and work with Product and Engineering to operationalize it.

• Help expand proven healthcare datasets across multiple customers instead of selling them once.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Work with Solutions and FDEs from the beginning of an opportunity.

• Coordinate with Healthcare Data Partnerships on sourcing and with Product and Engineering on tooling.

Required Experience & Skills

• Advanced degree (PhD or Master's plus 2+ years industry experience) in machine learning, computer science, biomedical informatics, epidemiology, statistics, or a related quantitative field — or equivalent applied experience.

• Hands-on experience building and evaluating ML or LLM-based systems for extraction, classification, or prediction on real-world data.

• Experience working with healthcare data: claims, EMR/EHR, clinical notes, imaging, registries, or similar. You understand why real-world clinical data is messy and what that means for model training.

• Strong Python and SQL, with the ability to work independently against large datasets.

• Experience designing evaluations — measuring data quality and dataset representativeness.

• Demonstrated ability to work directly with technical stakeholders and translate ambiguous goals into concrete, defensible research plans.

• Comfort operating on a customer's timeline without lowering the standard of the research.

Ideal Profile

The ideal candidate:

• Is energized by working directly with customers, and specifically by working with other researchers as peers.

• Moves fast on messy, real-world problems and knows which corners can and cannot be cut.

• Is rigorous about what the data can and cannot support, and willing to tell a customer when the answer is no.

• Enjoys the full arc — scoping a vague problem, doing the research, and showing the result to the person who asked for it.

• Thinks about leverage: builds the reusable version rather than the one-off when it's worth doing.

About DataLab

DataLab exists because truly useful data is rare — and the frontier of AI development only moves forward when high-quality data makes it possible.

We believe data is one of the most underdeveloped layers of the AI stack. Our work focuses on building and evaluating high-value datasets grounded in real-world workflows and economically meaningful tasks. Our research spans data quality, evaluation design, privacy-preserving transformation, and task-grounded AI training data.

• Partner closely with Product, DataLab, vertical GMs, and Sales to make sure our market story matches what we deliver to model builders.

About the Role

We're hiring our second attorney: a hands-on counsel who will work directly with the CLO and own a large share of Protege's day-to-day legal work. This is not a narrow specialist seat. On any given week you'll move between a data licensing agreement with a hospital system, a de-identification question under HIPAA, an NDA for a frontier lab, a vendor BAA, and a cross-border transfer analysis — often several of these in the same day.

The two areas where you'll spend most of your time:

  • Commercial contracts. Data license agreements, SOWs, NDAs, BAAs, DPAs, and vendor agreements — drafting, redlining, and negotiating with counterparties ranging from health systems and data aggregators to the largest AI builders in the world.

  • Data & Privacy. HIPAA/CCPA/GDPR and de-identification strategy, business associate posture, privacy policies, cross-border data transfers, and emerging AI regulation. Privacy at Protege isn't a compliance checkbox — it's core to the product on multiple domains.

You'll be the person our business, partnerships, and engineering teams come to first. The legal function here runs through Slack, Notion, and Google Drive, with other AI tooling built into triage and drafting. Requests come in fast, priorities shift, and much of the structure you'll work within is structure you'll help build.

What You’ll Do:

  • Draft, negotiate, and close commercial agreements across our data supply and demand sides — data licensing, SOWs, NDAs, BAAs, DPAs, and novel arrangements that don't have a template yet.

  • Counsel teams across the company on data privacy: HIPAA, de-identification, consent, provenance, GDPR/CCPA, and AI-specific regulation as it lands.

  • Triage and run a high-volume legal queue — dozens of active matters at a time — deciding what needs deep work, what needs a fast answer, and what needs outside counsel.

  • Work directly with technical teams and technical counterparties, translating between legal risk and how the product actually work–in plain and crisp communication style

  • Manage and coordinate outside counsel on specialist matters, keeping the work moving, tightly scoped, and the spend sensible.

  • Build the legal infrastructure as you go: templates, playbooks, intake, and AI-assisted workflows that make the whole function faster.

What Success Looks Like

30 days: Learn and Build Relationships

  • Meet and partner with the teams who use legal most — partnerships, BD, healthcare, product, and engineering — plus our outside counsel across commercial, privacy, and corporate, to understand intake, escalation paths, where the volume comes from, and where the bottlenecks are.

  • Get fluent in how we run: Slack-based intake, the Notion legal tracker, our template library, and the AI tooling we use for triage and drafting.

  • Take your first sets of NDAs, SOW redlines, and privacy questions end-to-end with CLO review.

60 days: Develop and Cultivate

  • Co-own the day-to-day commercial queue — NDAs, SOWs, DPAs, and BAAs move through you without hand-holding, at turnaround times the business can plan around. We optimize for speed and clarity.

  • Run your first data license negotiations end-to-end, from intake through signature.

  • Take ownership of at least one standing privacy workstream (e.g., de-identification posture, cross-border transfers, or privacy policy maintenance).

90 days: Make an Impact

  • Co-own the commercial and privacy queue, with the CLO engaged on strategy and novel structures.

  • Ship at least three improvements to our legal infrastructure — a template, playbook, or AI-assisted workflow — that measurably speeds up how legal work gets done here.

  • Be the trusted first call for the business: colleagues come to you directly, and get practical answers fast.

What You Bring

We care about what you've accomplished, not how many years you spent in a particular seat:

  • You've negotiated and closed complex technology or data transactions end-to-end — ideally including data licensing, and ideally opposite technical counterparties.

  • You've owned real pieces of a privacy program but see the whole picture and how it all hangs together: HIPAA and de-identification decisions, GDPR/CCPA compliance, DPAs and BAAs — not just reviewed someone else's work. And you keep up to date on emerging regulations and have a sense of not only where the puck is but where it’s going. Plus, you understand not just the what but the why behind key statutes.

  • You've run a high-volume legal queue where you were personally accountable for turnaround — you know how to triage, when 80% today beats 100% next week, and when to slow down because it matters.

  • You thrive in ambiguity and are proactive in finding the information you need to make informed decisions and guide the business forward.

  • You've operated in a fast-moving, scrappy, high-growth environment where priorities changed weekly and structure didn't exist until you built it — templates, playbooks, intake, or workflows that outlasted you. Extreme ownership is a mentality we embrace.

  • You work the way we work: Slack, Notion, Google Drive, and AI systems in daily use. Someone who works exclusively in Word attachments and email chains will struggle here; someone tech-native will thrive.

  • You bring high EQ to hard conversations — counseling colleagues under deadline pressure and negotiating across cultures and company sizes with practical, calm, solution-focused advice. You communicate in bullet points rather than paragraphs.

  • JD and active bar membership in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

What We're Looking For

Minimum qualifications:

  • 6+ years of relevant legal experience with significant depth in technology transactions and privacy (healthcare/HIPAA/GDPR/CCPA experience strongly preferred).

  • Speed and throughput. You turn documents fast, juggle many matters simultaneously, and know when 80% today beats 100% next week.

  • Genuine comfort with ambiguity. You're self-directed, you make judgment calls with incomplete information, and you don't wait to be handed a process — you build one.

  • Fluency with modern tools. Our legal work lives in Slack, Notion, and Google Drive, and we use AI systems daily for triage and drafting. Someone who works exclusively in Word attachments and email chains will struggle here; someone who's tech-native will thrive.

  • High EQ. You'll counsel colleagues under deadline pressure and negotiate with counterparties across cultures and company sizes. Practical, calm, solution-focused advice is the job. No jargon.

  • JD and active bar membership in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

Preferred qualifications — we encourage you to apply if you meet some but not all of these:

  • In-house experience at a technology company shipping products with novel legal risk, ideally involving AI, training data, or health data.

  • Experience negotiating data licensing agreements or other data-centric commercial deals.

  • Familiarity with de-identification standards (Expert Determination, Safe Harbor) and the healthcare data ecosystem.

CRM / Systems Ownership

  • Own Salesforce architecture, configuration, and long-term scalability

  • Lead ongoing phases of Salesforce buildout and manage relationships with implementation and systems partners as new capabilities are added

  • Establish structured change management and system governance

  • Evaluate, phase in, and integrate new GTM systems that support revenue operations as the stack grows — including the event/registration platform, the researcher community platform, and sales engagement tooling (Unify)

GTM Engineering & Automation

  • Build and maintain the automations and integrations that connect systems across the GTM stack, rather than relying on manual handoffs between tools

  • Use APIs, workflow automation platforms, and light scripting where native, declarative configuration isn't enough

  • Evaluate and pilot AI-enabled tools that improve GTM efficiency — lead scoring, data enrichment, forecasting support — and bring the ones that work into the core stack

  • Build durable systems designed to scale, not one-off fixes that create technical debt

  • Maintain data integrity and enforce required-field discipline

  • Prevent system sprawl and unnecessary customization as new tools are phased in

  • Establish documentation standards and clear ownership of system changes

  • Ensure Salesforce operates as the single system of record

  • Own the GTM data model, SQL/warehouse or BI layer, metric definitions, cohort analysis, funnel velocity, and executive reporting.

  • Define and operationalize qualification criteria and opportunity stage definitions

  • Design lifecycle processes spanning Marketing → Sales → Expansion, including multi-source lead handoff (event, researcher community, BDR, inbound), each with its own defined SLA

  • Standardize opportunity structure, pricing inputs, and partner attribution tracking

  • Ensure opportunity records accurately capture key economic inputs to support revenue and margin visibility

Forecasting & Pipeline Management

  • Design and maintain forecasting frameworks in partnership with the Head of GTM Operations

  • Establish and enforce pipeline standards and inspection cadence

  • Monitor stage progression, conversion rates, deal aging, and close probability integrity

  • Improve visibility into revenue realization assumptions and deal-level economics during forecasting

  • Identify structural bottlenecks impacting close rates and forecast reliability

  • Own researcher community systems and operations — onboarding flows, engagement tracking, and a defined path from active community member to sales-qualified lead

  • Administer the marketing automation platform and prospecting/sequencing tools (including Unify), keeping them integrated with the CRM

  • Own campaign QA and marketing database hygiene

  • Ensure multi-touch attribution integrity across events, researcher community, and digital — not a single-channel model — and full-funnel reporting accuracy

  • Build event-sourced pipeline and ROI reporting (cost per event, pipeline per event, win rate) and researcher community engagement and conversion reporting

  • Monitor marketing-to-sales conversion by source and identify structural bottlenecks

Be the Glue

  • Act as the connective, hands-on presence between Marketing and Sales — the day-to-day execution glue currently provided directly by the Head of GTM Operations, freeing that role up for strategy and cross-functional leadership

Company Overview:

We’re a lean, fast-moving, high-trust team of builders who are obsessed with velocity and impact. Our culture is built for people who thrive on ambiguity, own outcomes, and want to shape the future of data and AI.

About the team

The Human Data team produces the human judgments that make AI training data trustworthy. That includes annotating data, verifying model output, and the human review that makes healthcare data safe to use. We work with an in-house team of annotators and a network of partners ranging from annotation platforms to practicing physicians. Our work feeds the research teams building AI evaluations and training environments, and the AI labs that license our data.

About the role

You'll own human data projects from start to finish. A project might be 800 scanned medical documents reviewed by five annotators over three weeks, or thousands of physician ratings on model output for a research team. You scope it with the team that needs it, design and test the task, staff it, keep it on schedule and on budget, catch quality problems before they spread, and deliver results the customer can trust. This role is built for someone early in their career who wants to own outcomes quickly, and who is as comfortable in a spreadsheet as in a room with researchers.

What You'll Do

  • Own human data projects end to end: scope them with the requesting team, set timelines and budgets, and deliver on them.

  • Design tasks and instructions with the requesting team, and pilot them on a small batch before anything scales.

  • Staff projects across our in-house annotators and partner vendors, and manage those vendor relationships day to day.

  • Run calibration before production. Every annotator passes a known-answer test before their work counts, and anyone who doesn't gets feedback and a retry.

  • Track throughput, cost and quality by annotator and vendor, and report progress to leadership every week.

  • Catch problems early (an annotator drifting, a vendor slipping, an instruction that isn't working) and fix them before they reach the customer.

  • Handle sensitive data, including protected health information, under strict security procedures.

  • Travel on short notice when a project needs someone on site.

  • Make every project easier to run than the last one.

What Success Looks Like

  • 30 days: learn the machine. You've shadowed a live project, taken over its roster and returns intake, and met each of our annotation partners.

  • 60 days: own a project. You've taken one project from scoping to delivery on your own, and every open project is tracked in one place.

  • 90 days: own the portfolio. You're running two to three projects at once, you've scoped a new one directly with a requesting team, and you've delivered our first cost-and-quality comparison across vendors.

What You Bring

Must have

  • One to three years in consulting, finance, a startup, or another operationally intense environment where you owned complex projects with real stakes. Strong new grads with that kind of experience are welcome.

  • Strong analytical skills, with instincts for statistics

  • Comfort and experience with agentic coding/work tools, willingness to learn new ones

  • Comfort working directly with demanding stakeholders, including researchers and outside partners.

  • The judgment to notice when something is off and the instinct to raise it early rather than guess.

  • Clear, fast written communication.

  • Authorization to work in the U.S. as a W2 employee (required for access to protected health information).

Nice to have

  • Experience running data annotation, labeling or AI training data projects

  • Healthcare, clinical research or HIPAA-regulated work

  • Experience managing contractors, vendors or freelancers

  • Python or SQL

Pass the Loved Ones' Test. We act with integrity and do the right thing — especially when it's hard and no one is watching.

Always Find a Way. We are resourceful, resilient builders who solve hard problems and push through obstacles.

Go Fast and Grow Fast. Velocity matters. We move with urgency, learn quickly, and continuously improve as individuals and as a company.

Practice Kindness and Candor. We communicate directly and respectfully, building trust through honest feedback and genuine care for one another.

Deliver Together. We win as one team. Collaboration, accountability, and shared ownership drive our success.

Own the Outcome. Hone the Craft. We take pride in our work, sweat the details, and continuously raise the bar for excellence.

  • Prior authorization, utilization management, and referral operations

  • Scheduling, access, intake, registration, and care coordination

  • Provider network, credentialing, staffing, and practice operations

  • Contact center, patient/member communications, and service operations

  • Pharmacy, lab, imaging, and other healthcare workflow operations

  • Health plan, employer, third-party administrator, and population-health administration

  • Build a clear view of Protege’s active customer and prospect requests involving healthcare administrative and operations data.

  • Develop a practical market map of priority healthcare workflow categories, likely data holders, aggregators, brokers, and channel partners.

  • Create a prioritized view of immediate reactive sourcing needs and proactive healthcare partner categories, with clear owners, qualification questions, and next steps.

  • Independently run initial partner discovery and qualification conversations with strong notes, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through.

  • Consistently convert customer and prospect requests into actionable healthcare sourcing plans and qualified partner opportunities.

  • Move priority partners through data-rights review, privacy diligence, sample coordination, Data Lab feedback, and commercial evaluation with tight cross-functional coordination.

  • Demonstrate the ability to distinguish between a dataset that merely contains healthcare records and one that captures useful operational context, workflow sequence, or decision-relevant signals.

  • Support active deals by identifying viable supply paths, surfacing rights, privacy, quality, and delivery risks early, and keeping partner and internal stakeholders aligned.

It’s a startup, so things are messy – but it’s not many our first 0-to-1 startup rodeo for most of us.

Today, you’re someone who wants to be the “super IC” who combines the core marketing and growth fundamentals and first principles of the past decade and with the next gen marketing tools of today to drive outsized results.

You’re already experienced or familiar with the marketing waves the future — such as narrative new media, agentic workflows, cross-channel campaign building, community building, and IRL activations, to name a few — and you want to join a scaling AI company that recognizes the asymmetric advantage this gives those that ride the wave accordingly.

  • You love new media: you test new formats yourself, and you’re well versed in what hits online.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview:

We are building Protege to solve the biggest unmet need in AI — getting access to the right training data. The process today is time intensive, incredibly expensive, and often ends in failure. The Protege platform facilitates the secure, efficient, and privacy-centric exchange of AI training data.

Solving AI’s data problem is a generational opportunity. We’re backed by world-class investors and already powering partnerships with some of the most ambitious teams in AI. The company that succeeds will be one of the largest in AI — and in tech.

We’re a lean, fast-moving, high-trust team of builders who are obsessed with velocity and impact. Our culture is built for people who thrive on ambiguity, own outcomes, and want to shape the future of data and AI.

About the role

Healthcare data only becomes AI training data once patient privacy is protected to a standard an independent expert will certify, while keeping the clinical detail that makes it worth training on. Black out too little and patients are exposed. Black out too much and the data loses its value.

No single tool gets this right, because every dataset is different. A radiology report, a handwritten prior-authorization fax and a veterinarian's notes each fail in their own ways. So we've built a practice instead of a product. It combines off-the-shelf tools, custom rules, language models and human review, tunes the mix for each dataset, and proves the result with the kind of statistical validation an auditor would accept. It has cleared every recent independent review with zero failures.

You'll run it. You'll lead engagements from the first look at a new dataset to certified delivery, make the calls on what's safe to ship, and improve the method with every engagement.

What You'll Do

  • Lead data privacy projects from first look to certified delivery: assess the data, write the policy, tune the pipeline, validate, and deliver.

  • Design and run the experiments that decide which layers a dataset needs, measuring recall, over-redaction and cost for each.

  • Run validation the way an auditor would: set the pass bar before you look, test on fresh held-out samples, report confidence bounds, and never fix the test set.

  • Turn every miss into a lasting fix (a rule, a model or prompt change, or a human-review step) and lock it in with a regression test.

  • Work directly with independent expert determiners: prepare evidence, answer methodology questions, and respond to findings.

  • Direct human reviewers on the hard cases and adjudicate their disagreements.

  • Evaluate new tools and models (open-source NER, vendor APIs, models that run inside a partner's own environment) against our benchmarks.

  • Write down what you learn so the next engagement starts ahead of the last one.

What Success Looks Like

  • 30 days: learn the method. You know the playbook and tooling, you've shadowed a live engagement, and you've delivered your first intake assessment of a new partner's data.

  • 60 days: share the load. You've co-led an engagement through validation, owned the experiment that set its pipeline, and added new rules with regression tests.

  • 90 days: own it. You've led an engagement end to end, including the evidence package for the expert reviewer, and you've evaluated a candidate model with a clear keep-or-drop recommendation.

What You Bring

Must have

  • Minimum 2 years in data science, applied statistics, ML engineering, or quantitative research, working with real, messy data.

  • Solid statistics: sampling, confidence intervals, measurement design and inter-rater agreement. You can explain why a sample is big enough, and what it can't tell you.

  • Strong background, and experience using language models or AI coding tools to move fast.

  • Healthy skepticism. You verify claims before trusting them, including your own.

  • Clear writing for technical and non-technical readers, including external reviewers.

  • Authorization to work in the U.S. as a W2 employee (required for access to protected health information).

Nice to have

  • HIPAA de-identification experience (Safe Harbor or expert determination), or other privacy or healthcare data work

  • NER, OCR, clinical NLP or document processing

  • Working with auditors, regulators or external reviewers

  • Running annotation or labeling projects

The Role:

Build partnerships that bring differentiated wearable and consumer health data into AI development. You will combine domain expertise with commercial judgment to qualify partners, move datasets through evaluation, and grow the value of the portfolio.

What you will do

  • Qualify wearable device makers, consumer health apps, and other data owners across heart monitoring, fitness, sleep, nutrition, and metabolic health.

  • Assess what makes each dataset useful: sensor signals, sampling frequency, longitudinal coverage, device consistency, missing data, and available clinical or user-reported context.

  • Coordinate NDAs, representative samples, and DataLab review; translate findings into clear partner priorities and next steps.

  • Work with Commercial on pricing, licensing structures, and statements of work, and coordinate activation with Healthcare Operations and Solutions.

  • Maintain trusted partner relationships, surface underused data assets to internal teams, and develop partnerships that address customer demand and portfolio gaps.

What you bring

  • Experience in partnerships, business development, or data licensing within wearables or consumer health, with a track record of advancing external relationships into execution.

  • Working knowledge of continuous sensor metrics, activity and workout logs, user-reported data, and more; able to ask credible questions about quality, coverage, AI relevance, and licensing rights. Knowledge of the wearable and lifestyle data landscape and the platforms that hold differentiated datasets.

  • Ability to identify consent, privacy, and licensing questions and coordinate their resolution with the appropriate internal reviewers.

  • Strong prioritization, ownership mentality, and communication across commercial, technical, and operational teams; comfortable building structure in an early-stage environment.
